classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the larger sector’s arc as the new circle’s circumference, then solve for its radius.

inlines.text: Sean’s frisbee has a radius of 12 cm.
He cuts it into sectors of
and turns both into smaller frisbees.
The curved arc of each sector becomes the circumference of its new frisbee.
What is the radius of the bigger of the two new frisbees? Answer to 2 d.p.

answer.short: $6.75\text{ cm}$. The larger sector’s arc becomes the new frisbee’s circumference.
answer.worked:
The $202.5^\circ$ sector has the longer arc, so it makes the bigger frisbee. Let its arc length be $\ell$.
$$\begin{align*}\ell &= \frac{\theta}{360}\times2\pi R\\\ell &= \frac{202.5}{360}\times2\pi(12)\\\ell &= \frac{27\pi}{2}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
This arc becomes the circumference of the new frisbee.
$$\begin{align*}C &= 2\pi r\\\frac{27\pi}{2} &= 2\pi r\\\frac{27\pi/2}{2\pi} &= r\\r &= \frac{27}{4}\\r &= 6.75\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
